totals.deduplication: Focused candidate, diagnostic and earlier qualification runs are excluded from primary totals. Alternate-core replays are listed separately.

artifacts.retention: Generated C and manifests retained under unique labels; successful shared libraries are removed by the existing fixture.

review: Independent read-only review found and verified fixes for SegmentWritten loss across immediate legacy #DB, and required original descriptor fault probes plus backing-to-guest-fault-to-event-backing coverage. Final review of ecc5c3c22b found no remaining blocker within this unit; reviewer did not build or run tests.
native_findings: Every independent original stream uses a new KVM VM/vCPU, one initial SREGS write and no intermediate host mode rewrite. Reusing a vCPU after resetting RAM left stale TLB entries and a missing PML4.A update; that diagnostic fixture failure is retained and corrected without weakening RAM comparison.

Each SDK compares 144 original non64 MOV/LxS L/D metadata cases, 32 null FS/GS loads observed after an actual far jump into code64 and generated x64 C, and 16 descriptor fault cases on its primary core; alternate-core mode replays repeat them.

Both local hybrid core types report GP(selector) for a noncanonical descriptor start. A canonical start with a noncanonical tail reports GP(0) on core type 0x40 and GP(selector) on 0x20; both reject the complete range before a missing first-page translation, retain CR2 and leave the independent high page-table A bits unchanged.

The caller binds SelectorForStart or SelectorForRange explicitly. Runtime code never probes the host; the test oracle selects only its declared pinned core profile. Other processors remain unqualified.
The generated null-base observation stops before the raw terminal long HLT used only by the original CPU. This does not add a generated long-mode HLT implementation.
boundaries: Internal mixed-mode C++ embedding only; general compatibility function/source projection is not newly exposed. NeverC remains a host-x64 compiler, and Clang owns separate i386 source regressions.

Segment write receipts publish full caches or declared null base actions before event handoff. Completed linear accesses, watchpoint matches, empty paid journals and original instruction bytes survive backing repair without replaying accepted effects.
Non-CS L/D cache metadata never selects execution mode. Existing CS and descriptor privilege/type/present constraints remain in force.
The newly measured compatibility descriptor-tail policy must not be applied to code64 MOV/POP/LxS/IRET/RETF without independent original-byte evidence for those consumers.
Other non64 state-owner integrations, real/unreal/VM86 composition, software SMM/SGX and unbound event producers remain global gaps.
The supplied Actions runners previously exposed no SGX1/EPC/device and executed zero enclave instructions; this unit adds no physical SGX evidence.
No final LLVM release or production pin movement; neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6 and the LLVM gitlink remain unchanged.

cleanup.verification: Every decompressed archive member was hash-verified before superseded fixture directories were removed. Reports and active qualification artifacts remain available.
